name: return_without_action
description: The routine contains only a return, so it performs no work when entered. The reference run reached it, so it is a stub rather than substantive logic.

name: store_word_into_record
description: Writes the low word of the data register into a fixed field of a structure addressed by the address register, then returns. Its entry was not reached in the reference run, so it may be a fragment of a neighbouring routine.

name: decode_channel_command_word
description: Decodes a packed 32-bit command word into step and position values, stores the previous values in a per-channel record, and clears a run of bytes in that record. It also sets the DMA control register, so it manages audio DMA state for a channel.

name: copy_indexed_table_entry
description: Looks up a long word in a global table using an index held in a record. If the entry is zero it calls another routine and clears a flag byte; otherwise it writes the entry and a computed offset into an output record and sets the flag to all ones.

name: copy_block_from_table
description: Copies a block of long words from a global table, selected by an index in a record, into a destination buffer four long words per loop pass. It then stores the destination address and size into an output record and clears a flag byte.

name: load_table_entry_into_record
description: Selects a 152-byte entry from a global table using a one-based index and copies several of its fields into the caller's record, scaling one field by four. It also clears several per-channel state words.

name: copy_entry_fields_to_record
description: Copies the same set of fields from a source record into a target record, scaling one field by four and clearing several state words. It duplicates the field load used when a table entry is selected.

name: clear_record_status_fields
description: Sets four state words and one flag byte to zero. It resets the per-channel status fields so that playback starts from a neutral state.

name: update_four_audio_channels
description: Calls four channel routines in turn and references the audio location registers for all four Amiga channels. It acts as the top-level dispatcher that advances each channel once.

name: update_channel_period_tick
description: Advances one sound channel by one tick: applies slide and offset steps taken from lookup tables, clamps the result to a minimum of 113, and writes it and a sample pointer into the output record. Several counters in the channel record are decremented and reloaded when they expire.

name: run_channel_effect_command
description: Counts down a timer in a channel record and, when it expires, reloads it and runs one effect command chosen by a type field. The commands include negating bytes in the sample buffer, negating and shifting blocks of long words, adding a constant across a range, and further sample edits.

name: dispatch_through_jump_table
description: Performs an indirect call through a jump table that the decompiler could not recover, so its real targets are unknown from this evidence. It only forwards control to the table entry.

name: negate_byte_and_wrap
description: Negates one byte in a buffer addressed by the record, advances a stored offset, and resets the offset to its start field when it passes the end limit. It repeats the sign flip on each call.

name: return_minus_one_status
description: Returns the 32-bit value minus one and performs no other work. The result is a constant sentinel.

name: close_library_conditionally
description: Calls a close routine and, when the zero flag is clear, calls a second routine and then invokes a library function through a vector loaded from a global base pointer. It then makes one more routine call.

name: open_dos_library
description: Calls the exec library function OldOpenLibrary to open dos.library and stores the returned library handle in a global variable.

name: initialize_dos_and_port
description: Clears a block of working memory, opens the DOS library, allocates memory and takes the current-directory lock. It then sets up a message port, waits on it and handles incoming messages, calling three other routines along the way.

name: release_dos_resources
description: Optionally runs a callback, closes DOS handles and locks, frees memory, closes a library and replies to a message. It is the teardown counterpart of the setup routine.

name: release_linked_list_nodes
description: Walks a linked list of nodes, calls a routine through a stored pointer for each node to release it, then clears the list head and tail pointers. It returns zero.

name: parse_quoted_string_tokens
description: Splits a text buffer into tokens and skips blanks, tabs and newlines between them. Quoted tokens are unescaped: an asterisk followed by N becomes a newline, E becomes a control character, and asterisk followed by 0 ends the string. Up to 32 token pointers are stored in a table.

name: call_library_function_pointer
description: Loads a library base from a stack parameter and calls the function at a fixed negative vector offset from it. It is a thin wrapper that forwards the call to a library function.

name: return_empty_stub
description: The routine contains only a return and does no work. The reference run executed it, so it is a stub.

name: return_without_action
description: The routine contains only a return and does no work. It is called from the surrounding code and simply returns.

name: validate_lookup_result_status
description: Calls a lookup routine and returns minus one when it yields nothing. Otherwise it calls a routine with a flag argument when a bit in the result is set, calls a second routine, and returns minus one if a field in the context block is nonzero.

name: copy_text_with_space_limit
description: Copies a text string into an output buffer one character at a time while decrementing a remaining-space counter, calling a flush routine when the space runs out. The routine also references DOS input and output handles and a console window specification, so it is involved in console setup.

name: parse_device_and_path
description: Reads characters from a buffer, converting lowercase letters to uppercase when a flag bit is set, and checks for colon and slash separators. Its H branch scans a name up to a colon or slash, so it parses a device and path name.

name: prepare_stream_buffer
description: Obtains a new buffer through a routine when the stream has none or a reset flag is set. On failure it records error code 12 and returns minus one; on success it points the stream at the buffer and clears its flags.

name: write_byte_to_stream
description: Writes one byte to a buffered stream unless the stream is in an error or flushing state. It can switch the stream into write mode, obtains space through a routine when needed, and stores the byte while decrementing the remaining-count field.

name: read_byte_from_stream_entry
description: Returns the next byte from a buffered input stream by entering the shared read routine at its start. It returns minus one when no data is available.

name: read_byte_from_stream
description: Returns the next byte from a buffered input stream, refilling the buffer through a routine when it empties. It sets end-of-file or error flags when the routine reports zero or a negative result, and returns minus one in those cases. A carriage return byte is handled specially.

name: process_entries_in_reverse
description: Walks a table of eight-byte entries from the last entry back to the first. For each entry that is active and lacks a flag bit it calls a routine to process it.

name: copy_three_byte_fields
description: Copies a three-byte header from a source buffer, or from a default when none is set, into a fixed record. It then locates a following three-byte value and copies it too, clearing its flag when that value is empty.

name: append_limited_string
description: Appends characters from a source string to the end of a destination string, copying at most the limit given in the data register. It terminates the result with a zero byte.

name: copy_string_return_end
description: Copies a zero-terminated string to a destination and returns a pointer to the position of the terminator, so callers can append after it.

name: format_signed_decimal
description: Converts a signed number to decimal text: it writes a minus sign when the value is negative, collects the digits in a temporary buffer, then copies them back in reverse order and terminates the string. It returns the number of characters written.

name: parse_signed_decimal
description: Reads an optional sign and then decimal digits from a string, accumulates the value and stores it through a pointer. It returns the number of characters consumed.

name: insert_block_into_free_list
description: Returns a memory block to a sorted free list. The size is rounded up to a multiple of four with a minimum of eight, the block is merged with an adjacent free neighbour when they touch, and minus one is returned when it overlaps an existing free block.

name: chain_calls_with_check
description: Calls one routine and, if it returns nonzero, calls a second routine and returns minus one when a field in the context block is set. Otherwise it returns the second routine's result, or minus one when the first routine fails.

name: forward_argument_with_check
description: Passes its argument to a routine after a first check succeeds, then returns minus one when a field in the context block is set. It is the argument-forwarding form of the status-checking chain.

name: allocate_linked_list_node
description: Allocates a node of the requested size plus twelve bytes through a library memory call, stores the size and a link field in its header, and appends it to a linked list. It returns a pointer just past the header, or zero when allocation fails.

name: allocate_block_from_free_list
description: Allocates a block of at least the requested size from a sorted free list, rounding the size up to a multiple of four with a minimum of eight. It splits off the unused tail of a larger block and returns the block, or zero when the request is not positive.

name: process_pending_list_entries
description: Walks a linked list of entries and calls a routine on each entry that has one flag bit set, another flag bit clear, and differing stored values. It then makes one more routine call.

name: dos_call_with_error_code
description: Clears the error state and calls a DOS vector function. When that function returns minus one it reads the DOS error code, stores it, and sets an error status of five. It returns the call's result.

name: seek_file_with_error_capture
description: Clears the error state and calls a DOS seek function. On failure it records the DOS error code and sets an error status of twenty-two. When the argument equals two it issues one more seek call.

name: read_file_with_error_capture
description: Clears the error state and calls a DOS read function. When the read returns minus one it records the DOS error code and sets an error status of five, then returns the read result.

name: open_file_with_error_capture
description: Clears the error state and calls a DOS open function through its vector. On failure it records the DOS error code, sets an error status of two, and returns minus one.

name: open_file_if_unlocked
description: Calls a lock function on a name first. If the lock call returns nonzero it releases that lock and returns minus one; otherwise it opens the file and returns minus one with error status two when the open fails.

name: release_and_delete_file
description: Releases a lock on a name when one is present, then deletes the file and calls the delete routine. It then tries to open the name and records error status two with minus one when that fails.

name: close_file_handle
description: Calls a routine when a pending-state field is nonzero, then calls the DOS close function through its vector and returns zero.

name: multiply_fixed_point_values
description: Multiplies two 32-bit fixed-point values from data registers by summing the cross products of their 16-bit halves, shifting them into the high word, and adding the low-by-low product. It returns the low 32 bits of the product.

name: divide_signed_32bit_values
description: Divides one 32-bit signed value by another. It negates negative operands, normalises the divisor with shifts when it is wider than 16 bits, and applies the sign to the result before returning it.

name: divide_with_quotient_and_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor using normalised shift-and-subtract steps. It returns a 64-bit value that holds the quotient in its high half and the remainder in its low half.

name: copy_string_and_print_line
description: Copies up to seventy-nine characters from a length-prefixed string into a local buffer and terminates it. It looks up an entry and, when the entry has an associated value, writes the buffer to output followed by a newline and returns minus one.

name: echo_line_with_break_notice
description: Copies an input string into a local buffer and terminates it. It then looks up an entry and, when that entry has an associated value, writes the buffer and a newline to output and returns minus one. Its referenced text includes a break notice, so it also reports interruptions.

name: check_intuition_action_result
description: Looks up a library entry and passes it with two offset arguments and the values 250 and 60 to a routine. It returns zero only when that routine returns one, and its referenced text names intuition.library.

name: set_context_and_run_request
description: Stores a pointer into a context field, calls a routine with two offsets and the values 250 and 60, and returns zero only when the routine returns one.

name: stub_returns_zero
description: The decompiled body contains only a return of zero. The instruction listing and library references suggest more work, so the recovered code is a stub that cannot show it.

name: get_table_entry_pointer
description: Returns the address of an entry in an eight-byte-stride table when the index is in range and the entry is in use. Otherwise it records error status nine and returns zero.

name: check_disk_change_status
description: Reads a status word through a library vector and, when either of two status bits is set and a registered callback exists, invokes the callback. On success it clears the callback pointer and calls one more routine.

name: poll_entries_with_timeout
description: Loops over a table of entries that have a use flag set. For each entry not yet marked it reads a clock value and, when the clock exceeds the stored time by more than twenty thousand units, reallocates memory through the system and marks the entry. It returns one when any entry was marked and minus one otherwise.

name: scan_entries_and_free
description: Iterates a list of entries and, for each entry in use, copies a name into a stack buffer and calls several routines. Released entries are returned to memory through the system free call, and the routine references the text diskinfo.

name: send_port_message_and_wait
description: Allocates a message structure, fills in its node links and two data fields, and sends it through a message port. It then waits for a reply, retrieves it with a get-message call, and frees the message memory before returning the reply value.

name: process_pending_list_entries
description: Walks a linked list of entries and calls a routine on each entry that has one flag bit set, another flag bit clear, and differing stored values. It then makes one more routine call.

name: clear_entry_and_check_error
description: Looks up an entry and returns minus one when none exists. Otherwise it clears the entry's first word; when the entry lacks a flag bit it calls a routine first and returns minus one if the error field is set, while a flagged entry returns zero.

name: copy_text_with_space_limit
description: Copies a text string into an output buffer one character at a time while decrementing a remaining-space counter, calling a flush routine when the space runs out. The routine also references DOS input and output handles and a console window specification, so it is involved in console setup.

name: stub_no_pseudocode
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this routine, so its behaviour cannot be recovered. It is called by one other routine and its listing contains a single instruction.

name: append_path_separators
description: Appends a colon to a name when one is missing and the flag requests it. It then writes a path separator taken from a global setting when the buffer does not already end in a slash, colon or backslash, and terminates the result.

name: clear_and_release_request_block
description: Calls a release routine on an attached pointer when one is present, sets two state fields to minus one, and then calls two library functions through the global vector, one of which releases memory.

name: chain_calls_with_check
description: Calls one routine and, if it returns nonzero, calls a second routine and returns minus one when a field in the context block is set. Otherwise it returns the second routine's result, or minus one when the first routine fails.

name: validate_lookup_result_status
description: Calls a lookup routine and returns minus one when it yields nothing. Otherwise it calls a routine with a flag argument when a bit in the result is set, calls a second routine, and returns minus one if a field in the context block is nonzero.

name: build_request_record_flags
description: Looks up a request in a table and, when it can be created, sets a size field of the output record to 1024 or 2048 depending on a sign test of a stack value. It also copies two option bits into the record's flag byte.

name: claim_free_table_slot
description: Searches an eight-byte-stride table from its fourth entry onward for a free slot. When none is available it records error status twenty-four and returns minus one; otherwise it computes flags from its arguments and claims the slot.

name: expand_format_string
description: Copies text from a format string into the output buffer and, when it meets a percent sign, processes a conversion specifier from the stack arguments. It counts the characters written and returns that total.

name: append_string_unbounded
description: Advances to the terminator of a destination string and copies a source string onto its end, including its terminator.

name: queue_input_character_node
description: Reads one character through an input vector and, when the read succeeds, allocates a node and stores the character and a pointer in it. The node is linked into a list, and when no node can be allocated the input is released through a release routine.

name: multiply_fixed_point_values
description: Multiplies two 32-bit fixed-point values from data registers by summing the cross products of their 16-bit halves, shifting them into the high word, and adding the low-by-low product. It returns the low 32 bits of the product.

name: read_line_into_buffer
description: Copies characters from a source buffer into a destination until it reads a newline or the end marker, replacing the newline with a zero terminator. If the end is reached without a newline it terminates the buffer where it stopped.

name: stub_no_pseudocode
description: The decompiler timed out and produced no pseudo-code, so the behaviour cannot be recovered. The listing shows ten instructions that are referenced by absolute address, which is not enough evidence to name a purpose.

key: deuteros - the next millennium (1991)(activision)(m3)(disk 1 of 2)[cr skr]/Deuteros - The Next Millennium (1991)(Activision)(M3)(Disk 1 of 2)[cr SKR].adf:bootblock:0:000C
name: run_boot_disk_io_sequence
description: Runs as the boot block entry and issues a sequence of exec DoIO requests on an I/O request block. It sets the command and offset fields before each call and waits through a busy delay of fifty thousand iterations between them.

key: deuteros - the next millennium (1991)(activision)(m3)(disk 1 of 2)[cr skr]/Deuteros - The Next Millennium (1991)(Activision)(M3)(Disk 1 of 2)[cr SKR].adf:bootblock:0:00AA
name: issue_boot_read_request
description: Sets the command, data pointer, length and offset fields of an I/O request to the boot start code and issues it through the exec DoIO call. It then sets the command to a second value and calls one further routine.

name: call_and_return_register_value
description: Calls one routine and then returns the value held in a data register, which the call leaves unchanged. It is a small wrapper that passes that register back to its caller.

name: cycle_table_entries_into_slots
description: Advances a global index and, when it is nonzero, copies words selected from a table by that index into two destination slots. It then repeats the copy so that the slots cycle through successive table entries.

name: install_interrupt_server
description: Stores two constant bytes and two routine addresses into fixed global locations, then calls the exec library through a vector to add an interrupt server.

name: issue_io_request_command_nine
description: Sets the command field of an I/O request to nine, clears its offset field and a flag byte, and issues the request through the exec DoIO call.

name: issue_io_request_command_five
description: Sets the command field of an I/O request to five and clears its flag byte, then issues the request through the exec DoIO call.

name: issue_io_requests_in_chunks
description: Splits a large transfer into chunks of 5632 units, calling a routine for each full chunk. The remainder is issued as a command-nine I/O request before the routine returns.

name: issue_io_after_optional_step
description: Runs a routine when its argument is nonzero, then sets the I/O request command to nine, clears the flag byte, and issues the request through the exec DoIO call.

name: read_block_via_io_request
description: Sets up an I/O request with a buffer pointer and a length of 5632 and issues it through the exec DoIO call. When the request's flag byte is clear, it copies the buffer into the destination in long-word units.

name: copy_quarter_length_longs
description: Copies long words from a source buffer to a destination, with a count equal to a quarter of the byte count passed in the data register. It decrements the counter until it wraps.

name: run_io_pair_and_latch
description: Issues two I/O requests in sequence and then copies a long word from a fixed offset in a global block into a global variable.

name: compute_bitplane_region_offsets
description: Computes screen offsets for a region from a descriptor record, using a row stride of forty bytes and a screen of two hundred rows across four bitplanes.

name: update_row_offset_pointers
description: Stores a new value in a global when it differs from the last one and calls a routine to recompute dependent state. It then derives the screen offset for a row from a stride of forty bytes, handling negative and positive offsets separately.

name: reset_row_offset_pointers
description: Stores a new value, calls a routine to refresh a stored offset, and computes row pointers using a forty-byte stride. Negative row offsets return without changing the destination pointers.

name: merge_masked_bitplanes
description: Combines four bitplanes row by row with bitwise mask operations, writing each plane's result into the destination. The plane offset is 4000 words and the rows are advanced by the row stride.

name: blit_masked_bitplanes_clipped
description: Blits four bitplanes into a screen area, clipping the row count to two hundred rows. Source and destination are combined with mask operations in the same way as the adjacent merge routine.

name: decode_packed_bitplane_rows
description: Reads a descriptor record for a region and decodes packed bitplane data from a byte stream into the target planes. It uses a forty-byte row stride and clips the output to two hundred rows.

name: decode_bitplane_block_planes
description: Reads a descriptor record and decodes a block of packed bitplane data into the planes, writing the second plane at an offset of 32000 bytes. It shares its structure with the other packed bitplane decoders.

name: decode_control_byte_stream
description: Decodes a byte stream whose control byte selects between literal copies and repeat runs, writing byte pairs to the destination with a wrap-around stride. It calls an empty routine when the stream has no further work.

name: decode_flagged_byte_pairs
description: Decodes a stream of byte pairs where a flag bit in the control byte selects copy or repeat mode. Output is written with a wrap-around stride, and an empty routine is called to finish a run.

name: decode_masked_run_length
description: Decodes run-length coded bytes, using the low six bits of each control byte as a repeat count and writing the output with a wrap-around stride. Empty routines are called as part of the decode loop.

name: decode_repeat_byte_pairs
description: Writes byte pairs from the input stream to the destination with a wrap-around stride, decrementing a counter that tracks the remaining repeat count. It is an entry into the packed-stream decoder loop.

name: decode_planar_word_stream
description: Decodes a packed stream into sixteen-bit words for a block of bitplanes, deriving a count from the remaining width and storing it in a global variable. It writes through a word pointer and calls routines.

name: decode_stream_into_strided_rows
description: Decodes a stream whose control byte selects a literal or repeat mode, writing output into rows that advance by a fixed stride. A per-row length is taken from a table entry on each pass.

name: copy_or_repeat_word_pairs
description: Decodes a stream where bit six of the control byte selects between copying two bytes and repeating a following value. Output is written with a wrap-around stride.

name: decode_row_stream_with_counter
description: Decodes a row stream by reading a control byte and writing byte pairs with a row counter that decides when the stride wraps. It is the shared decoder body used by the packed bitplane routines.

name: decode_pairs_across_rows
description: Writes byte pairs from the stream across successive rows, decrementing a row counter and returning once it reaches zero. The destination pointer wraps when it passes the end of the buffer.

name: decode_rows_by_control_count
description: Decodes rows selected by a control count, copying byte pairs into each row and advancing the destination by a stride. It reloads the count from the stream when a row finishes.

name: decode_word_runs_with_mask
description: Decodes word-sized runs from a stream, where the low six bits of a control word give the run length. Each run is written as byte pairs with a wrap-around stride.

name: return_without_action
description: The routine contains only a return and does no work. Callers reach it through address-taken references, so it serves as an empty hook.

name: blit_masked_planes_by_offsets
description: Combines bitplanes row by row using a mask derived from four plane words, then writes each result back to the destination. The plane offsets are supplied in registers, and the row count comes from a second data register.

name: fill_tile_rows_and_mark
description: Stores the low byte of a working value and a record field, marks the record's first word as 65535, and fills rows of the screen buffer with a nested loop that steps forty bytes per row.

name: fill_clipped_tile_rows
description: Computes a row range from a record and a working value, clamping the end to row 199, and fills the matching forty-byte rows of the screen buffer.

name: build_offset_table
description: Copies a long word from a stack-relative location and clears a counter. It then walks a table of long words, computing an offset for each nonzero entry and storing the result in a second table.

name: rebase_offset_table_entries
description: Clears a counter and, for each of six table entries, adds a fixed base offset to nonzero values, storing the results in a second table. It then calls a library function through its vector.

name: update_timed_event_records
description: Walks a table of twenty-four-byte event records and, for each record with an active pointer, dispatches on its type code. Type three decrements a counter, other types call routines, and an inactive record has its pointer cleared.

name: scan_event_records_for_refresh
description: Decrements a countdown in the current record and steps through an array of twenty-four-byte records, calling a routine when the array is exhausted. For records with an active flag it counts them and compares their identifier with 255.

name: dispatch_event_by_type_code
description: Dispatches a record on its type code. Type five is handled when a stored counter matches and a position threshold is reached, type six reads a timing field and adjusts a position, and other codes call routines.

name: advance_record_position_by_step
description: For a type six record, decrements a counter and, when it is zero, adds the record's step amount to its position. It then continues with the next record in the array.

name: set_record_step_and_advance
description: Stores a new value into a record field and advances the record's position by its step amount. It then loops over subsequent records while their countdown fields are zero.

name: invoke_callback_for_type_twenty
description: When a record's type code is twenty and a callback pointer is set, it calls the callback and continues the record walk. Otherwise it moves on to the next record in the array.

name: clear_records_and_count_active
description: Clears the first long word of each record in an array of twenty-four-byte records and counts the records that are active. It also reads a custom chip register, so it is tied to hardware state.

name: accumulate_active_channel_flags
description: Walks an array of records and folds the value of each record whose flag word is nonzero into an accumulator. The accumulated result is stored in a global variable before a routine is called.

name: run_command_stream_step
description: Reads command words from a stream and dispatches on the low byte. Command three stores a value and a pointer into the channel record, and a zero word ends the stream by clearing the record's status word.

name: handle_stream_setup_commands
description: Reads command words in a loop and stores long-word operands into the channel record for command two. Command three sets a stream pointer and ends the loop.

name: store_word_and_long_operands
description: Processes operand commands in a loop: command two stores a long word into the record and command one stores a word. Other codes are handled by further branches.

name: store_word_and_set_global
description: Processes operand commands: command one stores a word into the record, and command four stores a word into a global variable and calls a routine through the global vector.

name: set_global_call_offset
description: Handles command four by storing a word into a global, then calling a routine through the global vector with an offset computed from a base constant. It repeats for the remaining operands.

name: store_long_and_return_pointer
description: Handles command five by storing a long word into the record and saving the operand pointer, then returns. Command six stores a long word and pointer in the same way.

name: store_long_pair_and_return
description: Handles command six by storing two long words and a pointer into the record and returning. Command seven adjusts a record field instead.

name: add_operand_to_record_fields
description: Adds a word operand to one of two record fields depending on the command code, then continues reading operands from the stream.

name: add_operand_or_jump_back
description: Handles command eight by adding a word operand to the second record field. Command nine moves the stream pointer back by a relative operand.

name: jump_back_or_combine_value
description: Handles command nine as a relative backward jump and command ten by calling a routine and combining its result with an operand, storing the result in the record.

name: store_masked_helper_value
description: Handles command ten by calling a routine, ANDing its result with an operand from the stream, and storing the masked value and a pointer in the record.

name: dispatch_commands_eleven_to_thirteen
description: Handles command eleven by calling a routine and advancing the operand pointer. Command twelve sets a pointer from an operand plus a base offset, and command thirteen performs further operand handling.

name: set_or_reload_operand_pointer
description: Handles command twelve by storing an operand-derived pointer into the record. Command thirteen reloads the stored pointer as the current stream position.

name: set_global_byte_from_operand
description: Handles command thirteen by reloading the record's stored stream pointer. Command fourteen stores a byte operand into a global variable.

name: store_base_offset_pointer_marker
description: Handles command fifteen by computing a pointer from an operand plus a fixed base offset, storing it in the record, and marking the record's first word with 254. Command fourteen stores a byte into a global variable.

name: set_pointer_and_clear_global
description: Handles command fifteen by storing a pointer computed from an operand, and command sixteen by setting a global word to 65535.

name: choose_random_masked_operand
description: Handles command seventeen by taking a value from a routine, masking it to its low four bits, and reducing it by a stored threshold. The loop continues until it meets command sixteen.

name: apply_random_nibble_offset
description: Handles command seventeen by drawing a returned value, masking it to four bits and adjusting it against a stored value. The adjusted value is then applied to the stream pointer.

name: dispatch_commands_eighteen_to_twenty
description: Dispatches command codes eighteen to twenty. Command nineteen sets a flag, and command twenty stores a command word and an operand pointer in the record for the surrounding loop to process.

name: loop_until_command_changes
description: While the command code equals eighteen, clears a flag and reads further commands in nested loops until the code changes.

name: store_operand_or_clear_field
description: Handles command twenty by storing the command word and an operand pointer in the record and returning. Any other command clears the record's first word.

name: clear_record_status_word
description: Clears one word in a record, the status field at offset six, and returns.

name: increment_and_clear_buffer
description: Increments a global counter and then clears 2000 groups of four long words starting at a global buffer pointer.

name: wait_for_hardware_flag
description: Calls a routine through a pointer offset from a global base, then busy-waits until a bit in a hardware status global is set. It blocks until that flag appears.

name: halt_in_infinite_loop
description: The listing contains only an infinite loop and performs no other work. Its evidence lists the background colour register, but the recovered body does not touch it.

name: poll_right_middle_buttons
description: Reads the right and middle mouse button state from the POTGOR hardware register, then calls seven routines that handle the result.

name: poll_fire_and_disk_status
description: Reads the CIA port A register, which holds the joystick and mouse fire buttons and the disk status, and calls four routines based on its value.

name: dispatch_two_input_routines
description: Calls two routines in turn and has little other work of its own. Parts of its body were removed as unreachable, so only the calls are recovered.

name: remove_interrupt_server_handler
description: Reads the CIA port A register for fire-button and disk status, then calls the exec RemIntServer stub to remove an interrupt server. Parts of the body were removed as unreachable.

name: remove_interrupt_server_mouse
description: Checks the right and middle mouse buttons in the POTGOR register and, depending on them, removes an interrupt server through the exec library stub. It also calls routines.

name: dispatch_two_helpers
description: Calls two routines in sequence with minimal work of its own. Most of the body was removed as unreachable code, so only the calls are recovered.

name: call_pair_of_routines
description: Calls a pair of routines with no further work of its own. The listing is short and the surrounding notes show removed unreachable blocks.

name: poll_until_magic_value
description: Loops until a checked value equals a fixed magic constant, calling a routine and polling a hardware flag on each pass. Afterwards it calls a library function with the argument 75776, runs a further routine, and stores two global values.

name: close_device_and_remove_port
description: Sets a state variable to one, closes a device and removes a message port through exec calls, and stores two global values. It also passes the argument 75776 to a library call.

name: clear_block_of_longs
description: Clears 2000 groups of four long words starting at a global buffer pointer. It writes zero in each group and advances by four long words per pass.

name: decrement_nibbles_each_tick
description: Sets a timing global to 256 and, on each tick once a hardware status bit is set, decrements the low four bits of each of fifteen words when they are nonzero. The words are then stored back into their array.

name: run_nibble_decrement_tick_loop
description: Runs the nibble-decrement tick loop after setting its timing global to 256 and clearing the tick counter. It calls a library function through its vector during the loop.

name: decrement_nibbles_each_tick
description: Waits for the hardware status bit on each tick, then decrements the low four bits of each of fifteen words when they are nonzero. The words are stored back into their array.

name: set_bit_and_reset_timer
description: Sets bit one of a control global, stores 256 in a timing global, then calls a routine.

name: initialize_music_player_state
description: Stores two pointers derived from a base pointer, clears a series of player globals, and sets a master value of fifteen. The four audio channels are prepared through their volume and DMA control registers.

name: update_channel_period_accumulators
description: Walks four-long channel records and, for each record with a nonzero first long, replaces that value and adjusts an accumulator by the difference. A step derived from a record field is then added, and records in one special mode receive a fixed value.

name: advance_channel_period_chain
description: Updates a chain of four-long channel records in sequence, replacing each value and adjusting its accumulator by the difference. Records in one special mode receive a fixed value, and each step adds a value derived from a record field.

name: reset_channel_volumes_and_dma
description: Sets the volume-register globals of all four audio channels to zero and a master value to fifteen. The DMA control register is among the registers this routine touches.

name: force_low_bit_and_call
description: When a status bit in a global is set, calls a routine, then calls another routine with the low bit of its data argument forced on.

name: advance_pattern_step_counter
description: Increments a tick counter and, when it reaches the stored tick limit, resets it and advances a step counter. When the step counter reaches sixty-five it wraps the pattern pointer forward by one entry and resets the step.

name: advance_pattern_row_pointer
description: When the step counter reaches sixty-five, advances the pattern position through its table and reloads the row address. It then increments the row address by sixteen bytes.

name: start_pattern_playback
description: Waits until a pattern table field is nonzero, points the row pointer at its entry, marks the player active, and calls eight routines before clearing a control global.

name: advance_row_and_run_channels
description: Advances the row pointer by sixteen bytes, calls eight routines in turn, and clears a control global.

name: apply_channel_command_word
description: Decodes a command word whose top nibble selects one of four audio channels. For the first mode it stores the channel's sample pointer and length fields from the channel table into the globals.

name: load_channel_zero_registers
description: Loads the sample pointer, length, period and volume values for audio channel zero from the channel table and writes them into that channel's hardware-state globals.

name: load_channel_one_registers
description: Handles two modes for audio channel one: mode two loads the sample pointer, length, period and volume from the channel table, and mode three stores a pointer for the channel.

name: load_channel_two_registers
description: Handles the third audio channel: mode three stores the sample pointer, length, period and volume from the channel table, and other modes store a pointer and clear a flag.

name: load_channel_three_registers
description: Loads the sample pointer, length, period and volume for the fourth audio channel from the channel table, and clears its status global.

name: apply_volume_effect_command
description: Decodes a command byte in which the middle nibble selects an effect. One effect negates the value, and another sets a channel volume or global depending on the channel index; a zero effect leaves the state unchanged.

name: set_player_flag_from_command
description: Handles three special command codes: code 2048 stores an operand in a global word, code 1536 clears bit one of a control global, and code 1792 sets that bit.

name: clear_or_set_control_bit
description: Clears bit one of a control global when the command code is 1536, and sets it when the code is 1792.

name: set_control_bit_on_code
description: Sets bit one of a control global when the command code is 1792.

name: set_channel_pattern_counter
description: Stores a decremented step count in a global and derives a pointer into the pattern table from it, then sets a control global to 64.

name: store_negated_value_by_index
description: Negates the data value and stores it in one of four player globals, chosen by an index in a data register. Index one selects the first global, two and three select the next two, and any other index selects the fourth.

name: store_value_three_way
description: Stores a value into one of three player globals chosen by an index in a data register. Index two and index three each select their own global, and any other index selects the default global.

name: store_value_if_index_three
description: Stores a value into a player global when the index is three, and otherwise into a default player global.

name: store_default_player_value
description: Stores the data-register value into a single player global without any index test.

name: store_value_four_way
description: Stores a value into one of four player globals, chosen by an index of one, two or three, with any other index selecting the fourth global.

name: store_value_two_way
description: Stores a value into one of three player globals based on an index of two or three; any other index selects the third global.

name: store_value_by_index_flag
description: Stores a value into a player global when the index is three, and otherwise into a second player global.

name: store_value_into_global_slot
description: Stores the data-register value into a fixed player global without any index test.

name: update_audio_channel_registers
description: Adds per-channel period and volume deltas to the player globals for all four audio channels, then writes the pointer, length, period and volume values to the audio hardware registers. When a flag bit is set it clears that bit and loads the next channel data, and it calls twelve routines to carry out the update.

name: add_table_byte_to_global
description: Reads a byte from a table addressed by a player global and adds it to that global, returning the masked sum. The decompiled body is a single add, so this is a fragment shared by several entry points rather than a complete routine.
